title: Question Words
summary: Ask basic questions with quem, o que, onde, quando, como, quanto, and por que.

sections.heading: Core question words
sections.body:
Brazilian Portuguese usually keeps the normal word order in questions and changes the intonation. Written questions use the question mark only at the end.

| Portuguese | English |
|---|---|
| quem | who |
| o que / que | what |
| onde | where |
| quando | when |
| como | how |
| quanto/a/os/as | how much/many |
| por que | why |

sections.heading: O que vs que
sections.body: Both **o que** and **que** can mean 'what'. **O que** is very common in full questions; **que** often appears before nouns or in fixed expressions.

examples.pt: Que tipo de música você gosta?
examples.en: What kind of music do you like?

sections.heading: Por que, porque, and por quê
sections.body: Use **por que** in questions and **porque** in answers. At the end of a question, use **por quê**.

examples.en: I study because I like Brazil.

keyPoints: Questions often use normal word order plus rising intonation.
Quem = who; onde = where; quando = when; como = how.
Use por que for 'why' and porque for 'because'.
Quanto agrees when it modifies a noun: quantas pessoas?
